name: Georgism
summary: Georgism, from the American economist Henry George, holds that people own what they produce but that land and natural resources belong to everyone, so the rent they yield should go to the community. Its main policy is a tax on the unimproved value of land that would replace taxes on labor, capital and trade, leaving land in private hands while socializing its rent. It pairs this with free trade and opposition to monopoly privilege, and some adherents would return surplus rent as a citizen's dividend.
scope: Classical Georgism as set out in Henry George's own books, speeches and journalism (Progress and Poverty 1879, The Land Question 1881, Social Problems 1883, Protection or Free Trade 1886, the 1887 Standard essay on socialism, A Perplexed Philosopher 1892), read with the scholarship on the single-tax movement. Modern Georgist organisations are used only where they state a position as their own. It excludes the anarchist and proprietary-community offshoots (Nock, Heath, MacCallum) and borrows nothing from the wider left, liberal or libertarian camps that have drawn on George.

notes:
Georgists split between a 'single tax limited' strand that would raise only what government needs and an 'unlimited' strand that would take all land rent. Domitrovic reports that Georgists later backed the progressive income tax and public ownership beyond the single tax, which George's own 1892 text condemns for income taxes; tax-the-wealthy is therefore recorded as a split. Themes searched in George's full texts: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. George's own texts record no position on immigration levels (his 1880 remarks and Protection or Free Trade treat Chinese labor competition only as a source of discontent and as a wage effect under present conditions), women's suffrage, the death penalty, drugs, abortion or sexuality, so those are null. A 2026-10-14 pass answered many such questions by inference; this pass keeps only stated positions and drops the old free-trade-adjacent and land-claims answers that rested on general values, including indigenous land authority and the earlier immigration, gradualism and social-issue answers.
